subject: Availability assurance addendum request + expansion pre-conditions
content:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finx.io>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: John Hansen <john.hansen@finx.io>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Repeated latency spikes — asking for assurance/addendum before renewal

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the trial capacity last quarter. Over the last 10 days we've seen intermittent latency spikes on our compute-heavy routes (tokenized invoices and document parsing). Spikes are short (~2-3 minutes) but severe enough to push our downstream workers into retries and increase our error budget.

Renewal is coming up for our account on Dec 15; we want to remain with Redwood, but our finance and platform teams are asking for a concrete availability assurance and a short-term remediation/compensation plan before signing the new 12-month commitment. Specifically, they're asking for:
- An addendum that includes a 99.95% availability SLO for our primary route (invoice-parse) and a clear credit table for miss events.
- A remediation plan and timeline for reducing the observed latency spikes (root cause report + mitigation steps).
- A path to move to Dedicated pools if the pilot demonstrates improvements, with pricing anchors.

I've attached a latency trace and a short timeline. Can you advise next steps and whether Redwood can provision an addendum for our renewal review?

Best,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, Finx

---
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finx.io>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Repeated latency spikes — asking for assurance/addendum before renewal

Hi Samir — thanks for the detailed notes and the traces. I'm sorry you're seeing those spikes. We take availability very seriously and want to get you a concrete proposal before your renewal.

Next steps from our side:
1) Marcus will triage the trace and provide an initial root-cause hypothesis by end of day tomorrow.
2) We'll propose a short-term operational play (prefix caching and route-level batching tweaks) to reduce transient spikes within 72 hours of agreement.
3) I'll draft an "Availability Addendum" that operationalizes a 99.95% SLO for your invoice-parse route, includes defined credit tiers, and a 30-day pilot-to-dedicated conversion path.

For transparency, if we agree to the 99.95% SLO for that single route, the addendum will include:
- Measurement window and exception carve-outs (regional outages, customer misconfiguration)
- Credit schedule: 5% credit for 99.90-99.95, 10% for 99.80-99.90, 20% below 99.80 for the affected billing period
- A 1-month stabilization period with weekly checkpoints

Can you confirm internal acceptance for a 30-day pilot-to-dedicated path? That affects pricing anchors.

Olga
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@finx.io>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Repeated latency spikes — asking for assurance/addendum before renewal

Samir, quick technical summary after an initial pass through the trace:
- Spikes appear correlated with large batch uploads from your OCR workers causing short-lived token-growth in a small set of shard replicas.
- We see KV-cache misses and cold-start spin-ups on a subset of inference workers during those windows.

Short-term mitigations we can apply immediately (low-risk):
- Enable route-level KV warmup for invoice-parse during your high-volume windows.
- Conservative batching caps for the affected model so single requests don't trigger large sequence allocations.
- Temporarily increase buffer capacity on the shard pool bound to your tenant for 72 hours while we monitor.

I'll prepare a short runbook and the instrumentation markers we will use to report SLO percentages. If the short-term mitigations don't bring the observed 99.95+ behavior, we recommend a 30-day dedicated pool pilot (isolated capacity) which historically eliminates noisy neighbor impacts in our infra.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

---
From: John Hansen <john.hansen@finx.io>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@finx.io>
Cc: Alicia Groves <alicia.groves@finx.io>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 11:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Repeated latency spikes — asking for assurance/addendum before renewal

Thanks, Marcus. The dedicated pilot is acceptable as a follow-up if mitigations don't move the needle, but finance needs:
- A pricing anchor for the 30-day dedicated pilot (expected CPU/GPU burn estimate + monthly committed price if we convert)
- A maximum credit cap for the quarter — they won't accept an open-ended exposure.

Can you include those in the addendum draft, or do we need a separate commercial term sheet?

John Hansen
VP of Finance, Finx

---
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: John Hansen <john.hansen@finx.io>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@finx.io>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Repeated latency spikes — asking for assurance/addendum before renewal

John — good point. Maya here (AE) and Sean (Sales Ops) is looped for pricing coordination. Proposed commercial approach we can include directly in the addendum: 
- 30-day dedicated pilot at a fixed pilot fee equal to 25% of estimated monthly committed price (pilot fee credited to the first month if you convert within 60 days).
- If SLO misses occur during the committed year, credit exposure capped at 30% of the annual committed value for that contract year.
- We will include a short appendix with a simple capacity/price example using your current token volumes (I'll attach the spreadsheet).

We can fold this into one addendum (operational SLO + short commercial appendix) so you have a single doc for legal/finance review. Olga — if that's okay, I'll prepare a draft and put it in the shared link, then route to Legal for a quick redline.

Thanks,
Maya Srinivasan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finx.io>, John Hansen <john.hansen@finx.io>, Alicia Groves <alicia.groves@finx.io>
Cc: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Repeated latency spikes — asking for assurance/addendum before renewal

Samir/John — thanks for the quick alignment. Action items we agreed: 
1) Marcus: apply the route-level KV warmup and batching cap changes within 24 hours and monitor a 72-hour window. Provide instrumentation markers to Finx.
2) Maya/Sean: publish the addendum draft (operational SLO + pilot commercial appendix) into the linked SharePoint by EOD tomorrow. Doc will include credit caps and pilot fee language.
3) Olga: schedule an exec review (30 minutes) for Dec 7 to review the addendum and the pilot pricing anchor.

If the 72-hour mitigation shows no improvement, we'll stand up the 30-day dedicated pilot within 7 business days and apply the pilot credit mechanics we discussed.

Appreciate the partnership — we'll aim to have a single addendum for legal by Dec 9 so you can sign ahead of your Dec 15 renewal.

Warmly,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: finx_latency_trace_1124.zip (log archive), proposed_availability_addendum_v1.pdf (draft), service-impact-timeline.xlsx (timeline + capacity example)
